title: Prefill token processing fastlane: reduce prefill-side overhead and introduce prefix-level caching and zero-copy paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce per-request prefill-side overhead for common prompt shapes by introducing a prefix-aware tokenization cache, zero-copy buffer reuse, and a fast-path that bypasses heavy parsing for short/templated prompts. Goal: reduce median prefill CPU time and p95 latency for small prompts used in chat and assistant flows.
background: Current runtime shows elevated per-request CPU on the prefill path: UTF-8 normalization, repeated encoder setup, and locking around a global tokenizer instance add ~1.2ms median and ~6-8ms p95 on typical short prompts. We've seen this amplify under high QPS and microbatching configurations. Prior tickets tackled tokenizer-prefill caching, but coverage is limited to large prefixes and implementations retained heavy synchronization.
success_metrics: tokenizer_prefill_latency_p50 <= 0.8ms for 1-40 token inputs; tokenizer_prefill_latency_p95 reduced by 40% for 1-200 token inputs; prefix_cache_hit_rate >= 65% for templated assistant prompts; no increase in memory OOM events attributable to cache
acceptance_criteria: 1) New prefix cache implemented with versioned keys and configurable size; 2) Zero-copy path exercised for small inputs with shared buffer reuse; 3) End to end testbench shows at least 30% median prefill latency reduction on standard chat load; 4) No regressions in decoding correctness; 5) Observability (metrics + dashboards) added and alerts for cache thrash; 6) Feature flag gated and rolloutable via console.
design_decisions:
- Use normalized fingerprint for cache key: (model_id, tokenizer_version, encoding_name, normalized_prompt_prefix, truncation_params).
- Cache tokenization outputs (token ids + attention mask + kv-prefillable metadata) rather than raw strings to avoid re-parsing.
- Implement per-worker tokenizers (pool) to remove global mutex contention.
- Provide zero-copy fast path for short ASCII/UTF-8 inputs: direct view into request buffer with borrowed lifetime semantics in Rust runtime.
- Eviction policy: LRU with size measured in tokens cached rather than entries.
- Cache invalidation via tokenizer_version bumping in model onboarding flow.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime changes live in runtime/tokenizer_pool. Prototype in rust branch ENG-14567/tokenizer-fastlane.
- Add ring buffer for per-worker request buffers to enable reuse and avoid allocations.
- For HF Tokenizers (Rust bindings), switch to non-blocking tokenizers where available; fall back to local pool.
- Expose cache config per-model in model manifest (max_tokens_cached, max_memory_mb).
- Add instrumentation hooks to measure cache hit/miss, serialization cost, lock-wait time.
- Keep feature behind experimental flag redwood.prefill_fastlane until Canary rollout.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for cache key normalization and versioning.
- Integration tests validating token id equality between cached path and cold-tokenize path across a matrix of tokenizers (BPE, SentencePiece, Unigram).
- Load tests using chat-sim harness (1000 rps sustained) to measure p50/p95 improvements.
- Regression tests for structured outputs (function calling payloads) to ensure tokenization context is preserved.
- Chaos test: rapid tokenizer_version rotations to validate eviction/invalidation logic.
rollout_plan:
1) Canary enable on 10% of hosted traffic for low-QPS tenants, monitor tokenization_latency_* and prefix_cache_hit_rate.
2) Expand to 50% after 48 hours with no regressions.
3) Enable in Dedicated clusters behind tunable config.
4) On private deployments provide opt-in CLI flag and docs.
5) After 2 weeks, promote feature flag to default for eligible models.
observability_changes:
- New metrics: tokenizer_prefill_latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}, prefix_cache_hit_rate, prefix_cache_evictions, tokenizer_pool_lock_wait_ms, buffer_reuse_rate.
- Dashboard: runtime > tokenization > prefill fastlane with breakdown by model and prompt-length bucket.
- Alerts: p95 increase > 25% or cache_hit_rate < 30% for > 10m.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Memory blowup from caching long prefixes: mitigate by token-count capped cache entries and per-model caps.
- Stale cache when tokenizer bugfixes occur: use tokenizer_version and release notes; immediate invalidation hook in model API.
- Concurrency bugs in tokenizer bindings: keep fallback to process-local single-shot tokenization and add runtime guard rails.
- Potential privacy/regulatory concern with caching user prompts: cache keys will use hashed normalized prefixes without storing raw PII; add opt-out flag for high-sensitivity customers.
progress_notes: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — prototype shows 0.9ms median vs 1.3ms baseline on 10k short prompts (node: chat-sim harness). Found tokenizer Mutex contention under >32 threads.
2026-02-28: Implemented per-worker tokenizer pool and ring buffer in prototype branch; microbenchmarks show a further 15% improvement.

2026-03-03: Discovered a correctness edge-case with SentencePiece normalization for non-breaking spaces; added normalization step to key generation and to cached token payload. Opened PR updating tokenizer bindings.
2026-03-07: Security review outcome: accept caching design with hashed prefix keys and opt-out for regulated tenants. Security approves experimental flag. (Reviewer: Miguel Torres)
2026-03-10: Integration tests green. Beginning controlled canary rollout for selected dev tenants under feature flag.
Next steps: finalize docs, create Console rollout UI, run 72-hour canary, collect metrics and decide on full rollout by 2026-03-24.

final_notes: This ticket targets commonly observed tail latency in prefill paths that disproportionately affects conversational customers. The plan balances CPU and memory tradeoffs while providing operational controls. If metrics exceed thresholds during canary, we'll roll back and split cache into shorter-prefix-only mode.
